content.text: I am able to replicated the bug with a test case now, which can prove SN-Sibling binary files are created and the javax.jcr.nodetype.ConstraintViolationException will be thrown when we are going to replace any of the SNS files. We are creating nt:folder for FedoraResource and nt:binary for FedoraBinary at this time, which should not allow SN-Sibling. But in this case Modeshape allows saving the binary files with SNS while thrown the weird exception when replacing one of the SNS files. So it looks more like a Modeshape bug but I think we can walk around it by disallow any new SN-Sibling files from saving to the binary store. Would you like me to create a PR to fix it for now?

Fedora is asking ModeShape to create resources that do not allow for SNS's.
I suggest we find a test that reproduces this at the ModeShape level. I will try to help creating such a test when I have the chance.
: As you know I've opened a

with a test that replicated the SNS issue we've seen. Horia Chiorean, the assignee of the MODE-2624 ticket, responses back that it's not a valid SNS test because we are asserting before calling session.save (see

), which indicates that the SNS path is just a temporal state and it'll gone after the file upload process is completed by calling session.cave. That explains why it's so hard to replicate the SNS issue on the ModeShape level. So I think the problem is partially related to our file upload process, which will ingest some metadata related to that file before calling session.save(). I am not sure whether Horia Chiorean will take any actions on the ModeShape level or not but I think the SNS problem should be solved if we change the ingest process to only ingest those file related metadata after the file ingest process is completed by calling session.save.
, That sounds like an interesting resolution. Have you been able to demonstrate at the Fedora level that splitting out the Binary and metadata updates addresses the issue?
is also looking at a solution in the context of:
I haven't tried to split out the binary and metadata updates yet but just thinking about it. But it looks like

's path locking solution should fix the SNS issue as well except that we should expect a ConstraintViolationException be thrown from the ModeShape level during ingesting while the path locking solution will not, which will try to ingest files to the same path one after one silently.
Do you think it's still worth us to spend some time to split out the binary and metadata updates to see how it goes or not?
's PR works out, and revisit the "split out" idea if necessary.

This is a bit of a two-parter, so it may need to be split into separate issues. I was using the Fedora 4 Vagrant image for testing this. First, to set up the conditions to reproduce this: from within the admin interface, when creating a binary resource, if the binary attachment is large enough, you can "double click" the "Add" button and it will create two instances of the resource. You end up with one resource called (assuming you named the resource such) "image_resource" and "image_resource[2]". You can also click multiple times to create additional resources indexed [3], [4], etc. I was also able to reproduce this with some clever cURLing, for both binary and container resource types. You have to do this on the initial transaction, however. Later attempts to duplicate the resource will result in expected error response. See:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/blob/master/fcrepo-kernel-modeshape/src/main/java/org/fcrepo/kernel/modeshape/services/BinaryServiceImpl.java#L62

Spec:
https://docs.adobe.com/content/docs/en/spec/jcr/1.0/6.7.22.8_nt_folder.html
https://docs.adobe.com/content/docs/en/spec/jcr/1.0/6.7.22.6_nt_file.html

I suggest we find a test that reproduces this at the ModeShape level. I will try to help creating such a test when I have the chance.

Andrew Wood: As you know I've opened a ModeShape ticket with a test that replicated the SNS issue we've seen. Horia Chiorean, the assignee of the MODE-2624 ticket, responses back that it's not a valid SNS test because we are asserting before calling session.save (see comment-13290375), which indicates that the SNS path is just a temporal state and it'll gone after the file upload process is completed by calling session.cave. That explains why it's so hard to replicate the SNS issue on the ModeShape level. So I think the problem is partially related to our file upload process, which will ingest some metadata related to that file before calling session.save(). I am not sure whether Horia Chiorean will take any actions on the ModeShape level or not but I think the SNS problem should be solved if we change the ingest process to only ingest those file related metadata after the file ingest process is completed by calling session.save.

Situ, Longshou, That sounds like an interesting resolution. Have you been able to demonstrate at the Fedora level that splitting out the Binary and metadata updates addresses the issue?

As a note, Michael Durbin is also looking at a solution in the context of: https://jira.duraspace.org/browse/FCREPO-2086

Hi Andrew,
I haven't tried to split out the binary and metadata updates yet but just thinking about it. But it looks like Michael Durbin's path locking solution should fix the SNS issue as well except that we should expect a ConstraintViolationException be thrown from the ModeShape level during ingesting while the path locking solution will not, which will try to ingest files to the same path one after one silently.
Do you think it's still worth us to spend some time to split out the binary and metadata updates to see how it goes or not?
Situ, Longshou, Let's see how Michael Durbin's PR works out, and revisit the "split out" idea if necessary.
It sounds good. Thanks.

This is a bit of a two-parter, so it may need to be split into separate issues. I was using the Fedora 4 Vagrant image for testing this. First, to set up the conditions to reproduce this: from within the admin interface, when creating a binary resource, if the binary attachment is large enough, you can "double click" the "Add" button and it will create two instances of the resource. You end up with one resource called (assuming you named the resource such) "image_resource" and "image_resource[2]". You can also click multiple times to create additional resources indexed [3], [4], etc. I was also able to reproduce this with some clever cURLing, for both binary and container resource types. You have to do this on the initial transaction, however. Later attempts to duplicate the resource will result in expected error response.
